evaluations.rationale: The incumbent pristine-tree portability result is established and needs no repetition. It is deferred because it cannot answer the remaining middleware fail-open question.

Selected. It turns the parser-level rejection into a server-boundary question: does the middleware return unauthenticated or treat the disabled result as anonymous? The disabled rejection is already observed, so this adds the downstream propagation evidence needed for the handoff.
Deferred and folded into the selected server check as the positive control. An enabled token must still put its subject into the handler context, proving the middleware is not over-blocking.
Deferred, not refuted. Project-role independence is already established at parser level; a middleware role control is useful but secondary to the disabled-account propagation question.

Deferred, not refuted. A concurrent toggle race needs a mutable settings store and many iterations. The predicate reads an account copy from an informer-backed store, so the simpler propagation test is higher value.

Deferred, not refuted. Line-ending portability is a real packaging concern, but the host applies the patch to a Linux source snapshot and the hunk context is small. It is less informative than the server-boundary check.
